_readme: The operator's address book — the whitelist. Copy it to data/book.json (the container
reads /data/book.json; TESTNET_PROTOCOLS_FILE names the path) or set TESTNET_PROTOCOLS
to the same JSON inline.
An entry is one of TWO KINDS, and 'kind' says which. 'vault' (the default) is a
contract that answers stake(uint256), withdraw(uint256) and publishes a record by
emitting YieldDistributed(uint256 indexed epoch, uint256 rateE18). 'aave-v3' is an
Aave v3 lending POOL: money goes in with supply(asset, amount, onBehalfOf,
referralCode) and comes out with withdraw(asset, amount, to).
A vault is priced from its own log: a record is what get_protocol_list() reads, the
YieldDistributed logs that address emitted in the last TESTNET_LOOKBACK blocks (5000 by
default). No log, no record, no price, no trade. An Aave pool emits nothing, so it is
priced from the feed's history of its 'pool' uuid — which is why that entry needs
TESTNET_HISTORY=auto (or =feed).
The difference is not decoration. A vault's address is a STRANGER until its own log
proves it implements the interface, so a feed-priced record about its name is never
signed. An Aave pool's address is proven by agent/physics/aave_v3.py instead: that
table files this pool and this asset under this chain id, the venue checks the pair
before any signature, and a pair it does not know is refused before the approval that
would have paid for it. That is the only reason an 'aave-v3' entry may be supplied on
a feed-priced record — and 'token' must name the asset the pool lends.
python -m agent.trade.loop --book-report
says it per entry, against the live chain and the live market, and exits 4 when
nothing can be priced.
Each entry carries a 'pool' — the DeFiLlama uuid of the pool this address actually
implements, which is what lets TESTNET_HISTORY=auto (or =feed) price it from the
feed's own daily history instead of a name guess. Both uuids below were read out of
https://yields.llama.fi/pools and checked against the address: the Aave row's
underlyingTokens[0] is the USDC it lends, and the Uniswap row is the 0.05% WETH-USDC
pool this address is (see poolMeta). With 'pool' pinned the entry needs no name match
at all; without it, 'name' has to be spelled like the pool.
Keys the loader reads: address, name, bucket, claim_apy, decimals, token, note, pool,
kind, project, symbol, chain.
address   0x + 40 hex — the vault, or (kind aave-v3) the lending POOL. Checked, and
lower-cased. For Aave it is the Pool, NOT the aToken: the pool is what
pulls the asset and what a withdraw is sent to, and the aToken is only the
receipt the position grows into.
name      the label a human reads: 'aave-v3 USDC (Arbitrum)' or anything else. It is
still the first thing the cycle matches on (normalised: letters and digits).
project,
symbol,
chain     the entry's identity in the FEED's own words — DeFiLlama spells the Aave
row project 'aave-v3', symbol 'USDC', chain 'Arbitrum'. A label and a feed
row are written for different readers and drift apart, so these three are
what a match needs: with them, an Aave pool is recognised by what it IS
rather than by how its name is spelled. For 'kind: aave-v3' they are also
checked against agent/physics/aave_v3.py before anything is signed — a book
that pins symbol 'USDT' on the USDC pool is refused, because it would be
matching another row's verdict. Leave any of them empty to match nothing.
A vault ignores them: its address is a stranger until its own log speaks.
bucket    safe | active | experimental (agent.physics.portfolio.BUCKETS).
decimals  credits per token unit: 6 for USDC, 18 for an 18-decimal token.
token     the ERC20 the venue pulls: on stake() for a vault, as supply's asset for
an Aave pool (where it is required — the wrong asset supplies the wrong
coin). Empty means the built-in default for a vault.
kind      vault (default) | aave-v3. The venue checks an aave-v3 pair against its
deployment table, by the chain id the node reports, and refuses the entry
if the pair is not in it — so this key cannot be used to point the loop at
arbitrary contract.
pool      optional DeFiLlama pool uuid: pins which pool prices this entry, so the
feed fallback matches a uuid instead of a label. Empty means 'match the
name', which is a heuristic the operator declares by spelling it well.
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by the loader and exist for the reader.

_template_for_your_vault.name: USDC
_template_for_your_vault.note: the vault this loop is allowed to stake into, and nothing else

protocols.name: aave-v3 USDC (Arbitrum)
protocols.note: the Aave v3 Pool on Arbitrum One, over native USDC — a real, audited protocol, and the one entry this loop can supply on a feed-priced record because the deployment table in agent/physics/aave_v3.py names it by chain id; the receipt is aUSDC (0x724dc807…8c637), the pool uuid is DeFiLlama's aave-v3 USDC (Arbitrum), and project/symbol/chain are how the feed spells that same row

protocols.name: uniswap-v3 WETH-USDC (Arbitrum)
protocols.note: Uniswap V3 USDC/WETH 0.05% pool on Arbitrum (read back from the factory's getPool) — not a vault of this interface and not an Aave pool, so it stays a diagnosis: the record is the feed's and the loop holds it; the pool uuid is DeFiLlama's uniswap-v3 WETH-USDC (Arbitrum, 0.05%). Its project/symbol/chain are declared for the report's sake and are never used to sign: only an aave-v3 entry may be matched by declaration
